we_do_better: Techniques vs. tools distinction — we separate reusable methods (Skills) from products (Tools), which no competitor does; this is uniquely valuable for practitioners
Source transparency — video quality badges, low-quality flags, and endorsement counts let users judge credibility at a glance; competitors show no provenance
MCP/connector tracking — dedicated Connectors tab covering MCP servers is a niche no competitor addresses
Live RSS news feed merged with video-sourced news, covering 50+ authoritative AI sources alongside the playlist
Self-improvement system and open audit trail (merge log, deleted skills, suggestion queue) — competitors are static catalogs that never explain their curation choices
Fully free, open-source, no ads, no paywall
they_do_better: Visual thumbnails and tool logos — Future Tools, Product Hunt AI, and Toolify show product images; our wall of text cards is harder to scan quickly
Item-count badges per category — Future Tools and TAAFT display count per filter tab; users immediately know scope before clicking
Simultaneous multi-axis filtering — Toolify lets users filter by category + pricing + rating at once; we only support category filter per tab
Hero section and featured/trending slots — all four competitors surface a 'start here' section; we drop visitors into an unlabelled card list
Sort controls — competitors offer newest / top-rated / most-popular sort; our Skills and Tools tabs only sort by quality score with no user control
User-generated signals — Product Hunt shows upvotes and comments; TAAFT shows verified-user saves; our popularity is editorial (video endorsement counts), not crowd-sourced
borrow_next: Add item-count badges to tab buttons (e.g. 'Skills (38)', 'Tools (89)') — one line of JS per tab, high discoverability signal at zero cost
Add a sort toggle (Quality | Mentions | Newest) to the Skills and Tools tabs — ~15 lines of JS, eliminates the main gap vs Toolify/Future Tools for power users

Add a 2-sentence 'What is Excavatortron?' tagline beneath the H1, and pin the top-3 starred skills to the top of the Skills tab as a 'Featured' strip — teaches new visitors what they're looking at without a tutorial

findings.detail: TODAY = datetime(2026, 6, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc) is hardcoded at module level. The recency penalty function compute_age_months() subtracts video age from this frozen date, so all recency penalties calculated after June 3 2026 are wrong — videos will appear progressively older than they are, inflating penalties and depressing quality scores over time. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Replace with datetime.now(timezone.utc) (computed inside compute_age_months or at call time, not module level), exactly as src/fetch.py does.

findings.detail: load_json and save_json open files without encoding='utf-8'. Hebrew transcripts and Unicode tool names (common in this playlist) will cause UnicodeDecodeError/UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 default-locale runners. src/fetch.py uses encoding='utf-8' consistently; analyze_batch.py does not. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to every open() call in load_json (line 152) and save_json (line 160).

findings.detail: process_video.py has its own duplicated load_json/save_json (lines 16–28) with the same missing encoding='utf-8' as analyze_batch.py. Additionally, _write_skill_md() at line 318 opens the SKILL.md output file with bare open() — no encoding='utf-8'. All three locations will fail on Hebrew-sourced or Unicode-named content. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to load_json (line 19), save_json (line 24), and _write_skill_md (line 318) in process_video.py. Consolidate load_json/save_json into a shared src/utils.py to prevent the divergence from recurring.

findings.detail: no_transcript=78, new_found=78 in status.json — a 100% transcript fallback rate. Every single new video from the last fetch fell through to description or title, meaning 78 videos were analyzed from shallow metadata only. The broad except-all in fetch_transcript() silently swallows any library or API failure. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Log the exception at WARNING level before falling back. Add a health check: if no_transcript / new_found > 0.5 for a run, set a flag in status.json and show an amber banner in the dashboard. Verify installed youtube-transcript-api version compatibility with the dual-API branch in fetch_transcript().

findings.detail: describe_tool() returns a hardcoded category-keyed string regardless of video content. Every new tool extracted uses this function, so the same template is injected into both skills.json and tools.json for every new tool. WORSENED: now 38 of 89 tools (43%) have template descriptions, up from ~5 noted last run — each new analyze run makes this worse. Root cause still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Replace describe_tool() with extraction from the transcript: use the 1–2 sentences in the video that most concisely describe what the tool does. If no sentence qualifies, set description to null and show 'Description not yet extracted' in the dashboard.

findings.detail: 'Anthropic' is catalogued as a tool (6/10, 73× mentions) with the description 'Anthropic is an AI tool by Anthropic. It enhances productivity through AI-powered features and automation.' Anthropic is the company, not a product. Its tool-card is misleading and inflates the tools count with a non-tool entry. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'anthropic' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into the 'claude' tool entry (Anthropic's product). Add to improvement_suggestions.json as a safe_auto merge.

findings.detail: 'Openai' is catalogued as a tool (6/10, 45× mentions) with the same generic template description. OpenAI is the company; its products (ChatGPT, DALL-E, GPT-4) already have their own entries. Having 'openai' as a separate tool creates confusion and duplicate credit. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'openai' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into 'chatgpt'. Raise a suggestion for the improve stage to auto-merge.

findings.where: data/tools.json — 38 of 89 entries (43%) have template descriptions
findings.detail: 38 tool entries now use the describe_tool() template pattern ('It enhances productivity through AI-powered features and automation', 'It assists with software development', 'It automates workflows', etc.). This has WORSENED from ~5 noted last run — the root cause (describe_tool() in src/analyze_batch.py) is still unfixed and every new analyze run injects more fake descriptions. 43% of the Tools tab shows zero real information.
findings.suggestion: Fix describe_tool() in src/analyze_batch.py to extract real content from transcripts (see finding e5a3f8b2c7). The improve stage's fill_missing_summaries module should back-fill existing template descriptions with real content where transcripts are available.

findings.detail: Every skill record generated by analyze_batch.py has three hollow template fields: use_case ('Using {tool} for {category} tasks.'), output ('{tool} produces {category}-focused outputs.'), and relevance ('{tool} is featured as an AI tool in this video.'). These add no information and inflate the card view. The CLAUDE.md spec says use_case should be 'primary use case as shown in the video'. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Extract use_case and relevance from the transcript using the same sentence-extraction approach as extract_tips(). If no qualifying sentence is found, use null/empty rather than a template.

findings.where: data/weekly_news.json (75 empty) + data/monthly_news.json (91 empty) + data/daily_news.json (3 empty)
findings.detail: 169 video news entries have empty summaries showing '(summary pending)' in the News tab. This count is UNCHANGED from last run — neither the improve stage's fill_missing_summaries module nor the analyze stage is making progress on the backlog. The root cause (no_transcript=78 for new videos) means 78 newly classified news entries have no transcript to summarize from.
findings.suggestion: The improve stage's fill_missing_summaries safe_auto module should prioritize the weekly/monthly backlog. For videos with only description/title, generate a 1-sentence summary from the description text. Address the transcript-failure root cause (finding 8a1b5c4d6e) so future fetches have real content.

findings.detail: MCP connector detection uses a hardcoded list of only 8 specific string patterns (filesystem, browser, github, postgres, sqlite, memory, slack, google drive). Any other MCP server mentioned in a video is silently ignored. CLAUDE.md Step 8 specifies exhaustive MCP hunting. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Broaden detection: capture any pattern matching 'npx .+-mcp', 'uvx .+-mcp', 'mcpServers', 'smithery', or 'mcp.so' in the text as a generic MCP connector, extracting the name from the matched string.

findings.detail: Slash-command regex r'/[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,20}\b' matches URL path segments (/api, /v1, /s3), common prose slashes, and file paths. The exclusion list only blocks 14 single-character tokens. Over a playlist of 900+ videos this accumulates false-positive commands in commands.json. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add a context requirement: only record a slash command if it appears adjacent to known AI tool names or follows a clear command-demonstration phrase. Extend the blocklist to common path prefixes (/api, /v1, /v2, /src, /static, /docs).

findings.detail: The tool is stored as 'Chatgpt' (wrong casing) instead of the correct brand name 'ChatGPT'. This is the 3rd most-mentioned tool and the casing error appears in the dashboard for every visitor. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Rename name to 'ChatGPT' in data/tools.json. One-line fix.

findings.detail: fetch_playlist_videos calls request.execute() with no retry or error handling for YouTube API quota exhaustion (HttpError 429/503). If the quota is hit mid-pagination (playlist has 1054 items across ~21 pages), the function raises an unhandled exception and the entire fetch run fails. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Wrap request.execute() in a retry loop with exponential backoff for 429/503, up to 3 attempts, before re-raising.

findings.detail: write_skill_md() in both analyze_batch.py (line 402) and process_video.py (line 318) opens SKILL.md output files with bare open() — no encoding='utf-8'. Additionally, main() in analyze_batch.py opens pending JSON files (lines 725-726, 747-748) without encoding. Hebrew content or Unicode tool names will cause UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 runners. The encoding bug runs throughout multiple files.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to all remaining open() calls: analyze_batch.py lines 402, 725-726, 747-748 and process_video.py line 318. Then do a global search for 'open(' in both files and verify each has explicit encoding.

findings.detail: In git_commit_push(), the retry loop calls git pull without checking its return code. If the pull fails (e.g., merge conflict, authentication failure), the code continues and retries git push on a broken state, exhausting all 3 retries with no diagnosis. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Check the return code of the git pull: if it != 0, log the stderr and break/return early. Example: pr2 = subprocess.run(...); if pr2.returncode != 0: return f'pull failed: {pr2.stderr[:100]}'.

findings.detail: The most-mentioned tool (Claude, 402×) is shown with a generic template description as the first card on the Tools tab. The highest-traffic entry communicates no actual information. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Fix the source data (replace template descriptions) AND add a UI guard: if a tool description matches the known template pattern, show a 'Description pending' pill instead of the filler text.

findings.detail: Tab buttons show no item count. Competitors (Future Tools, TAAFT) display per-category counts. The dashboard now shows 38 skills and 89 tools but the nav buttons say nothing, making the catalog feel sparse. Note: status.total_skills is stale (10), so live item counts must be read from the loaded data, not status. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: After loading each tab's data in the init() async block, inject item counts into nav buttons: e.g. 'Skills (38)', 'Tools (89)', 'Connectors (8)'. ~10 lines of JS. Read counts from loaded JSON arrays, not status.json.

findings.detail: Skills and Tools tabs have no sort control. Users can only filter by category; they cannot sort by newest, by mentions, or reverse quality order. All four benchmark competitors offer multi-axis sort. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add a sort <select> or pill-toggle above the card list: Quality (default) | Mentions | Newest. Implement as a client-side sort on the already-loaded array. ~20 lines of JS.

findings.detail: No hero tagline or onboarding copy explains what Excavatortron is. First-time visitors see 'Excavatortron — AI Skills Tracker' and a search box with no context. All four competitors have a 2-3 sentence value proposition above the fold. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add one sentence beneath the subtitle: 'Tracks AI techniques, tools, models, and MCP connectors extracted from a curated YouTube playlist — updated automatically, quality-scored, and searchable.'

findings.detail: Inline Python in both workflows uses datetime.datetime.utcnow() which is deprecated in Python 3.12+ and will emit DeprecationWarning. When GitHub Actions upgrades to Python 3.13+, this may become a hard error. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Replace datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z' with datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() in both workflow inline scripts.

findings.detail: renderAlert builds el.innerHTML = msg where msg contains raw HTML tags hardcoded in JS alongside esc(status.token_hint). The esc() call protects the dynamic value, but the pattern (mixing safe-markup with partially-escaped content) is fragile — a future maintainer adding another dynamic field may forget esc() and introduce stored XSS. Data comes from repo-committed JSON (low external risk), but the pattern is worth fixing. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Build the alert using DOM methods (createElement, textContent) rather than innerHTML, or create a dedicated safe-template function that always escapes dynamic values and keeps static HTML separate.

findings.detail: main() always sorts pending records newest-first (reverse=True), regardless of the workflow's order instruction. The analyze.yml workflow passes 'order=oldest_first' during normal mode and only switches to newest_first during catch-up. But analyze_batch.py ignores this entirely — it has no order parameter and always processes newest-first. CLAUDE.md Step 1 specifies oldest_first for the normal default. This causes older pending videos to be processed last indefinitely, and the 'oldest_first' contract with the user is silently violated.
findings.suggestion: Add an --order argument to analyze_batch.py (default: 'oldest_first'). When order=='oldest_first', sort by publishedAt ascending. Pass the workflow's order value via the script argument or an environment variable. Update analyze.yml to pass the order to the script.

findings.detail: /tmp/sorted_pending.json is written on the first call and reused on subsequent calls within the same runner environment. GitHub Actions may reuse warm runners for the */30 sprint crons. If the file exists from a previous run, newly added pending videos are absent from the list and won't be processed until the file is regenerated. The file is never deleted. This is a latent but real correctness hazard for any runner that handles back-to-back analyze jobs.
findings.suggestion: Delete /tmp/sorted_pending.json at the start of every main() invocation before checking if it exists, or unconditionally regenerate it on each call. The file serves only to avoid re-scanning _pending/ within one run — rescan on every run is cheap and correct.

findings.detail: status.total_skills is 10 but skills.json actually contains 38 skills. The dashboard counter 'Total skills' shows 10, which is wrong by 73%. The field is set by fetch.py from the skills file at fetch time, but analyze_batch.py adds skills during the analyze stage without updating status.total_skills. So the counter is always stale and understates the actual count.
findings.suggestion: In process_video() (analyze_batch.py and process_video.py), update status['total_skills'] = len(skills_data['skills']) after saving skills.json. Or compute it lazily in the dashboard from the loaded skills array length rather than status.total_skills.
